sources.name: High-Pressure Crystal Structure Database
sources.notes: The initial HPCSD release reports 77,346 static high-pressure structures spanning 89 elements. The public portal redirects to sign-in and the paper states that additional data are available on request; do not scrape authenticated pages.

sources.name: HOFSyn hydrogen-bonded organic framework structures and synthesis
sources.notes: The raw and P1-standardized archives each contain 631 actual CIF files; the synthesis/property table has 660 rows. The 2.35 GB literature-PDF archive and EndNote export are not crystal structure/property records and are intentionally excluded.

sources.name: opXRD open experimental powder X-ray diffraction database
sources.notes: The verified archive contains exactly 92,552 JSON pattern records and no frame or trajectory files. A content scan found 912 labels with complete lattice plus atomic basis, 1,267 partial phase labels, and 90,373 unlabeled experimental patterns.

sources.name: SIMPOD simulated powder X-ray diffraction open database
sources.notes: Structures.zip contains the source structure and simulated one-dimensional diffraction record. Its 467,861 entries pass a full Python Zip64 decompression and CRC scan; legacy Info-ZIP 6.00 misreads this very large Zip64 central directory. The 29.4 GB radial-image rendering and two redundant 5.9/20.5 GB CSV exports are excluded to preserve SSD space without losing the structure/property records.

sources.name: High-Throughput Screening Platform for Solid Electrolytes
sources.license: CC BY 4.0 record; underlying ICSD-derived structures retain ICSD terms
sources.notes: The verified archive contains 91,763 newline-delimited static structure records plus BVSE, CAVD, conduction-descriptor, and literature-property tables. Its 49 hierarchical calculation records include migration-path coordinate arrays; those arrays are not structures and are explicitly excluded from MateriaViva ingestion. No images or frame files are present. The code archive is excluded, and ICSD-derived structures remain local-only under their source licence.

sources.name: SuperBand electronic-band and Fermi-surface database of superconductors
sources.notes: The full Science Data Bank HDF5 and the accompanying GitHub snapshot are collected. Structures originate mainly from Materials Project and OQMD and will be matched later; SuperBand-specific band and Fermi-surface properties are retained.

sources.name: Atomly materials science database
sources.license: Atomly service terms and source-dataset provenance
sources.notes: Bulk acquisition running via scripts/datasets/atomly.py with account session token (documented 120 req/min per-IP limit; API keys are scoped to 5 read-only endpoints at 10/min+200/day, OPTIMADE endpoint exists but is not deployed yet). Phases: chemical-system enumeration (search_by_elements, 100-row cap, recursive subdivision), detail harvest (get_struct_detail per struct id: lattice, energies, symmetry, prim/conv CIF, electronic diagram), blind sweep of the dense id block [1,150000] for capped-system overflow. Sparse id blocks near 1e9/3e9 are only reachable via enumeration.

sources.name: MatCraft Materials API
sources.license: MatCraft terms of service and upstream MP, AFLOW, and JARVIS provenance
sources.notes: Documented records aggregate MP, AFLOW, and JARVIS structures already collected here. sources.name: PowBase powder diffraction database

sources.name: NIST Crystal Data
sources.notes: The published NIST-3 release contains 237,671 crystallographic records. No open bulk redistribution path was found; obtain the licensed database from NIST or through an institutional subscription.

sources.name: NIST Surface Structure Database
sources.notes: The current NIST release reports nearly 1,400 experimentally determined surface structures. It is legacy licensed software/data rather than an open bulk download; contact NIST for access before ingestion.

sources.name: NIMS MDR harmonic phonon calculation database
sources.notes: The NIMS collection exposes 10,034 per-material datasets but no collection-level bulk archive. Each phonopy_params.yaml.xz contains the initial static unit cell plus harmonic phonon displacement/force data. MateriaViva will create only one static structure record per MP material ID; displacement supercells are property inputs, not structures or trajectories. Request a bulk snapshot instead of issuing roughly 10,000 record-page and file requests.

sources.name: ELEMENTA and ELEMENTA Spin
sources.notes: Fetched with huggingface_hub at revision 9de9010715da4f563326f99bf3f7ee829cf4486a, which is the revision recorded in the local HF download cache; both archives match the remote x-linked-size exactly and both pass a full zstd stream check. The dataset card declares cc-by-nc-4.0 and the repository is public and ungated. This is trajectory data: 38,808,603 frames over 2,028,008 relaxations in the core archive and 4,713,110 frames over 207,185 relaxations in the spin archive. Under section 7 rule 3 only the endpoint of each relaxation enters the structure pool and every intermediate ionic step is discarded. Trajectory identity is the (material, structure, spin) triple rather than material alone: partway through the spin archive the material tag drops its spin suffix, so consecutive magnetic runs share one tag while restarting ionic_step at zero, and keying on material alone silently merges those runs and loses about 62 percent of that archive. CC BY-NC 4.0 restricts the whole published snapshot to non-commercial use.

sources.name: Carolina Materials Database
sources.notes: The provider site (http://www.carolinamatdb.org/, Jianjun Hu and Ming Hu groups, University of South Carolina) states 214,436 inorganic materials (16,302 ternary, 198,134 quaternary) and licenses the data CC BY 4.0, confirmed verbatim on both the landing page and /terms/. It serves plain HTTP only; the HTTPS listener returns a malformed TLS record, so official_url is not reachable over TLS. The site publishes no bulk archive, no REST API and no OPTIMADE endpoint, and is absent from the OPTIMADE provider registry; /download/ has never existed in the Wayback record. Its only machine-readable routes are one static VASP POSCAR per record at /static/export/vasp/{primitive_cell,conventional_cell}/<i> for i in 0..214435, and the HTML detail page /entry/<i+1>/ carrying formation energy per atom, cell volume and the space-group assignment. Search results paginate at 10 rows and require a session POST, so a full mirror would cost about 236,000 requests at roughly 1.3 s each. The acquired copy therefore comes from the two CC BY 4.0 bulk redistributions instead: the MatSciML benchmark deposit (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.8381476, v1.0.0, 2023-08-31) whose carolina_matdb.zip holds an LMDB of 214,435 records with cell parameters, atomic numbers, Cartesian coordinates, space group and a per-atom formation energy; and the ColabFit Exchange curation of that same deposit (DOI 10.60732/f2f98394, 214,267 configurations) which preserves the LMDB key in its names field. The legacy /home/zhilong/SSD/material_data/carolina_matdb_structs.lmdb is that same Zenodo release re-serialised as pymatgen Structure dicts: all 214,435 keys match and all 214,435 records agree on composition and lattice, but the legacy copy dropped the formation energy. Neither bulk snapshot carries the site's CMD-ID, so records cannot be linked back to /entry/ pages without re-deriving the mapping.
